questions.q: What is the shape of Scheduling's symptom, compared to Billing's?
options: Several sessions start fine and then just stop mid-request for minutes — the signature of blocking, not a bad plan
One query that runs the same amount of time every single execution
A query that returns the wrong results, not a slow one
A query that fails with a syntax error
questions.explain: Scheduling's calendar freezing is sessions stalling mid-request, which points to blocking rather than a bad execution plan.

questions.q: What does querying sys.dm_exec_requests WHERE blocking_session_id <> 0 reveal during the freeze?
options: Several scheduling sessions all waiting on the same one blocking_session_id
That no sessions are connected to OverlookClinicalDB at all
That the Billing invoice query is the cause
That dbo.Appointments has no rows in it
questions.explain: Several different scheduling sessions all show the same blocking_session_id, pointing to one session at the head of the chain.

questions.q: What identifies the session actually responsible for the blocking chain?
options: The one session whose own blocking_session_id is 0, with open_tran_count showing an uncommitted transaction
The session with the lowest session_id number
The session that most recently connected
Any session with status = 'sleeping'
questions.explain: The head of the chain has blocking_session_id = 0 in its own row and open_tran_count = 1, meaning it holds an open, uncommitted transaction.

questions.q: What is the batch job actually doing that keeps its transaction open so long?
options: It updates appointment statuses, then waits to commit until it finishes sending confirmation messages for every row
It is running a CREATE INDEX statement that takes minutes to complete
It is performing a full database backup during business hours
It never actually opens a transaction at all
questions.explain: The job reads and updates appointments, but delays committing until a separate, slower message-sending step finishes for every row, holding locks the whole time.

questions.q: Why is this a genuinely different root cause than Billing's missing index?
options: The batch job's query plan may be fine — the problem is duration, a transaction staying open across an unrelated slow step
It is actually the exact same missing-index problem as Billing's
It only affects the dbo.Invoices table
It can be fixed with the same CREATE INDEX statement from Lesson 7
questions.explain: Nothing about this is a missing index or bad plan — it's a transaction held open too long while locks block everyone else.
